text:
These non-magical tricksters delight in bamboozling
their dim-witted opponents and pride themselves on
how many times an actual spellcaster has tried and
failed to counterspell them.

When you choose this archetype at 3rd level,
you gain proficiencywith playing cards and
either Sleight of Hand or Performance. Your
proficiency bonus is doubled for any ability
check you make that uses these proficiencies

Starting at 3rd level, you may use your
Cunning Action to attempt to Dazzle creatures
with a trick.
Choose up to 2 creatures lower on the
initiative order than you, that are within 25ft
and can see you.
They must make Wisdom Saves against your
Dazzle DC (8+Dexterity modifier+proficiency
bonus) or become incapacitated until the end
of their next turn. You can Dazzle twice per
combat, the second time creatures make the
save with advantage.

Creatures with True Sight have disadvantage
on the save the first time you attempt to
Dazzle them as their precautions against
magical illusions backfire when faced with this
non-magical trick.

Starting at 9th level, you can make your foes
believe you can disappear behind a puff of
smoke(or dragon fire).
When you use your Evasion feature you can
immediately move up to half of your
movement speed and attempt to Hide.

At 13th level, when you use Sneak Attack on a
surprised victim, a creature of your choice
within 30ft that can see you must make a
Intelligence Save against your Dazzle DC or be
stunned until the end of their next turn.
If that creature is also surprised it has
disadvantage on the save.

Starting at 17th level, you can use your action
to put on a show.
Any creatures of your choice within 30ft of
you, that can see you, must make a
Intelligence Save Vs your Dazzle DC or be
surprised until the end of their next turn.
Creatures can be affected by surprise this way
no matter what round it is.

Surprised creatures can’t move or take actions
and can’t take a Reaction until their turn ends.
You can do this once between long rests.
